children.value: > Fact From Story: Epic sued Google in 2020 after a fight over in-app purchase fees, claiming the Android operating system’s Google Play Store constituted an unlawful monopoly
> > Fact From Story: Google requires apps to use its own first-party billing system, and charges app developers a 15% to 30% commission on the sales it processes.

> > > Fact From Story: Google will counter Epic’s arguments by pointing out that it has rolled out a new option for app developers called User Choice Billing, which Epic has declined to use. | Supporting Fact
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Companies generally prefer to avoid paying high fees. | Supporting Fact
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Companies generally prefer to avoid paying high fees.

> Fact From Story: Fortnite maker Epic Games is still set to go to trial with the tech giant today, November 6, in hopes of convincing a jury that Google engages in anticompetitive behavior with regard to its Android app store, Google Play, and its commission structure.
> > Fact From Story: Google will counter Epic’s arguments by pointing out that it has rolled out a new option for app developers called User Choice Billing, which Epic has declined to use.
> > > Fact From Story: Epic sued Google in 2020 after a fight over in-app purchase fees, claiming the Android operating system’s Google Play Store constituted an unlawful monopoly
> > > Fact From Story: Google requires apps to use its own first-party billing system, and charges app developers a 15% to 30% commission on the sales it processes.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Companies generally prefer to avoid paying high fees.
> > Fact From Story: Google requires apps to use its own first-party billing system, and charges app developers a 15% to 30% commission on the sales it processes.

> > > Fact From Story: This case will differ slightly from Epic’s battle with Apple on the same topic because, this time, Epic can’t allege there’s no other way to load apps onto Android devices, as it could with Apple, because Android does allow for sideloading apps.
> > > Fact From Story: Google will counter Epic’s arguments by pointing out that it has rolled out a new option for app developers called User Choice Billing, which Epic has declined to use.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: A company is more likely to sue another company if they believe they are being harmed by them.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Companies generally prefer to avoid paying high fees.
> Commonsense Knowledge: Antitrust laws are designed to prevent anticompetitive behavior.
